375646.title: TxGraffiti's annihilation-number bound for connected graphs
375646.statement:
Let $G$ be a nontrivial connected graph. Write $4\alpha(G)4$ for its independence number, $4a(G)4$ for its annihilation number, $4R(G)4$ for its residue, and $4\Delta(G)4$ for its maximum degree.

**TxGraffiti's conjecture.** One has

$$
\alpha(G) \ge \frac{a(G)+R(G)}{\Delta(G)},
$$

and this bound is sharp.

The conjecture is open in general; it is established for regular bipartite and cubic Kőnig–Egerváry graphs. The bound is motivated by automated graph conjecturing and is sharp, for example, for the complete graph on four vertices.

375646.analysis: Conjecture 1 and Theorem 2 proof: a is the longest sorted degree head of sum at most m; R is the final Havel-Hakimi zero count. K2 exception explicitly appears in source. Caro-Wei argument resolves connected Delta>=2. Automated provenance and already printed exception preclude credit.

record.domain: All connected unlabelled simple graphs, orders 2..7

375666.title: Dasgupta–Kárólyi–Serra–Szegedy conjecture for distinct products in finite abelian groups
375666.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|>1$, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$. Let $k<p$, let $a_1,\ldots,a_k\in G$ be pairwise distinct, and let $b_1,\ldots,b_k\in G$. **Dasgupta–Kárólyi–Serra–Szegedy conjecture.** There is a permutation $\sigma\in S_k$ such that

$$
a_1b_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,a_kb_{\sigma(k)}
$$

are pairwise distinct. This extends the corresponding theorem for cyclic groups of prime-power order and elementary abelian groups. The conjecture is presented as a proposed extension of those results; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
375666.review_depth: literal statement, raw provenance, bounded history/title screen, primary conjecture/theorem text; selected proof-body reading specified in note
375666.analysis: Source Conjecture 1.1 allows repeated b entries and assumes k<p(G). Theorem 1.3 settles abelian p-groups; the general mixed-prime case is not supplied. Exhaustive symmetry-reduced k=4 tests in C35 and C55 address mixed-prime cases beyond the stated factorial-prime criterion. Need a general transversal argument for arbitrary finite abelian groups, including noncyclic mixed Sylow factors.

record.domain: Cyclic groups C_n, 2<=n<=15; 1<=k<min(p,4); unordered distinct a and multiset b (permutation symmetry)

375727.title: Girao, Kittipassorn, and Narayanan's long-cycle conjecture
375727.statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree $\delta(G)\geq 3$, and suppose that $G$ contains a Hamiltonian cycle. **Girao, Kittipassorn, and Narayanan's conjecture.** There exists a constant $c>0$ such that $G$ contains another cycle of length at least $n-c$. Girao, Kittipassorn, and Narayanan proved a polynomial-error version with loss $cn^{4/5}$; the paper improves this to loss $cn^{2/3}$, but the constant-error assertion remains open.
375727.review_depth: literal statement, raw provenance, bounded history/title screen, primary conjecture/theorem text; selected proof-body reading specified in note

Finite c=1 checks do not prove any uniform constant; need an unbounded-deficit family or a uniform cycle-switching argument.

375753.title: Faudree–Gyárfás–Schelp–Tuza strong clique index conjecture
375753.statement:
For a finite simple graph $G$, let $L(G)$ denote its line graph, let $G^2$ denote the graph in which two vertices are adjacent exactly when they are at distance at most two in $G$, let $\omega$ denote clique number, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$. **Faudree–Gyárfás–Schelp–Tuza conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\omega(L(G)^2) \le \frac{5}{4}\Delta(G)^2.
$$

This is a weaker counterpart to the Erdős–Nešetřil conjecture for the strong chromatic index. It is tight for blow-ups of $C_5$ and remains open; the best-known general upper bound stated in the paper is $\frac{4}{3}\Delta(G)^2$.

record.domain: All unlabelled simple graphs, orders 1..7

375755.title: Cambie–Cames van Batenburg–Joannis de Verclos–Kang conjecture for $h_3(\Delta)$
375755.statement:
For positive integers $\Delta$ and $t$, let $h_t(\Delta)$ be the smallest integer such that every graph $G$ with at least $h_t(\Delta)$ edges and maximum degree $\Delta(G)\le \Delta$ contains two edges at distance at least $t$. **Cambie–Cames van Batenburg–Joannis de Verclos–Kang conjecture.**

$$
h_3(\Delta)\le \Delta^3-\Delta^2+\Delta+2.
$$

This concerns the next case of the edge degree-diameter problem after the solved $t=2$ case. The paper states it as an open conjecture and notes that blow-ups of $C_5$ provide tight examples for the preceding case.

375817.title: The $q,t$-dihedral sieving conjecture for cluster parking functions
375817.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Dih}_{n+2}$ act on the diagonal coinvariants $A/I$, and let $\varDelta$ denote their bigraded character as a character of $\mathfrak{S}_n$ polynomially depending on $q$ and $t$. Let $\Lambda$ be the character of $\operatorname{Dih}_{n+2}\times\mathfrak{S}_n$ on $\tilde H_{n-2}(\operatorname{CPF}_n)$, and let $\Sigma$ be the specified sign character of $\operatorname{Dih}_{n+2}$ extended to the product. For $\mathbf{F}\in\operatorname{Dih}_{n+2}$, write $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ for the eigenvalues of the defining representation $\rho_1(\mathbf{F})\in O(\mathbb{R}^2)$.

**The $q,t$-dihedral sieving conjecture.** For every $\mathbf{F}\in\operatorname{Dih}_{n+2}$ and $\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_n$,

$$
(\Lambda\Sigma)(\mathbf{F},\sigma)=\left.\varDelta(\sigma)\right\vert_{q=\lambda_1,\ t=\lambda_2}.
$$

This is the $q,t$-symmetric-function formulation of the preceding character identity and is intended as a homological dihedral sieving phenomenon. The supplied text says that its extension beyond symmetric groups is difficult because a sufficiently developed $q,t$-combinatorics is lacking.
375817.review_depth: literal statement, raw provenance, bounded history/title screen, primary conjecture/theorem text; selected proof-body reading specified in note
375817.analysis: Source Conjecture 1.4 is equivalent to 1.3. Rank n>=2 comes from setup. Sigma is Definition 8.1, not an arbitrary twist. No small chain-complex/coinvariant implementation was completed. Need actual dihedral action, homology and bigraded quotient computations before a valid finite search. This remains an explicit unmet search requirement.

375866.title: Reed's chromatic bound conjecture
375866.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ and clique number $\omega(G)$. **Reed's conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi(G) \leq \left\lceil \frac{1}{2}(\Delta(G)+1+\omega(G))\right\rceil.
$$

This refines the Borodin–Kostochka direction and is equivalent to a stronger interpolation between maximum degree and clique number. It remains open, although partial results establish related bounds with a smaller coefficient than the conjectured one.

375867.title: Kawarabayashi–Picasarri-Arrieta dichromatic bound conjecture
375867.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph. Define

$$
\widetilde{\Delta}(D)=\max_{v\in V(D)}\sqrt{d^-(v)d^+(v)},
$$

and let $\overset{\text{tiny}}{\leftrightarrow}{\omega}(D)$ be the largest size of a biclique in $D$. Let $\vec{\chi}(D)$ denote the dichromatic number of $D$. **Kawarabayashi–Picasarri-Arrieta conjecture.** Every digraph $D$ satisfies

$$
\vec{\chi}(D) \leq \left\lceil \frac{1}{2}\left(\widetilde{\Delta}(D)+1+\overset{\text{tiny}}{\leftrightarrow}{\omega}(D)\right)\right\rceil.
$$

If true, this would imply Reed's conjecture and an independent conjecture of Harutyunyan and Mohar. The conjecture is presented as open in the source.
375867.review_depth: literal statement, raw provenance, bounded history/title screen, primary conjecture/theorem text; selected proof-body reading specified in note
375867.analysis: Digraphs are loopless, may contain digons; biclique is a bidirected complete subdigraph. Parameter is max sqrt(indegree*outdegree), not max outdegree. Exact dichromatic partitions tested to order4, with floating square root only for small integer rounding diagnostic; no universal proof.

record.domain: All labelled loopless digraphs on 1..4 vertices, all 2^(n(n-1)) arc sets

375879.title: Erdős Matching Conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
375879.statement:
Let $M_s^r$ be a matching of size $s$ in an $r$-uniform hypergraph, and let $\operatorname{ex}_r(n,M_s^r)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no copy of $M_s^r$. **Erdős Matching Conjecture.** For integers $s,r\geq 2$ and $n\geq sr-1$, 

$$
\operatorname{ex}_r(n,M_s^r)\leq \max\left\{\binom{sr-1}{r},\binom{n}{r}-\binom{n-s+1}{r}\right\}.
$$

This conjecture extends the Erdős–Gallai theorem from graphs to uniform hypergraphs and predicts the extremal number for forbidding a matching of size $s$. The paper describes its main theorem as a spectral confirmation in the sufficiently large-$n$ regime, while the full extremal conjecture is not stated as completely resolved here.
375879.review_depth: literal statement, raw provenance, bounded history/title screen, primary conjecture/theorem text; selected proof-body reading specified in note
375879.analysis: The forbidden matching has s edges and hypergraphs are r-uniform; n>=sr-1. All edge subsets to order5 tested, source only proves sufficiently large-n spectral regime. Need arbitrary intermediate-n extremal argument.

record.domain: All r-uniform hypergraphs on labelled n=2..5, r=2..n; all nonvacuous s with n>=sr-1

375901.title: The maximality conjecture for nm-independence on Polish groups
375901.statement:
Let $G$ be a Polish group. An **nm-independent relation** is the relation $\mathrel{\raise0.2ex\text{\ooalign{\hidewidth$\vert$\hidewidth\cr\raise-0.9ex\text{$\smile$}}}}^{nm}$ defined by non-meagerness of the corresponding product of stabilizer sets. A **strongly admissible geometry** on $G$ is an independence geometry induced by an ideal scheme and satisfying the strong admissibility conditions.

**The maximality conjecture.** The relation $\mathrel{\raise0.2ex\text{\ooalign{\hidewidth$\vert$\hidewidth\cr\raise-0.9ex\text{$\smile$}}}}^{nm}$ is the maximum strongly admissible geometry on $G$.

If true, this would show that nm-independence is intrinsic among strongly admissible geometries for Polish groups. The source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

375905.title: The maximal product-of-trees embedding conjecture for handlebody groups
375905.statement:
Let $F_2$ be the free group of rank $2$, let $F_2^n$ denote its $n$-fold direct product, and let $\mathcal{H}_g$ be the handlebody group of genus $g$. A subgroup or map is **quasi-isometrically embedded** when the induced orbit map, equivalently the inclusion with respect to word metrics, is a quasi-isometric embedding. **Maximal embedding conjecture.** The maximal integer $n$ such that $F_2^n$ quasi-isometrically embeds into $\mathcal{H}_g$ is

$$
n=g-1.
$$

This asks for the largest number of independent free-group factors that can occur in a quasi-isometric embedding into the handlebody group. The surrounding discussion identifies this as a main question arising from the paper's work; no resolution is stated here.

Source reduces upper bound to incompatibility of all one-holed tori, using Definition 3.5 and Corollary 3.6. That incompatibility remains the precise gap; small genus exceptions cannot earn credit.

375920.title: Boltyanskii's illumination conjecture for convex bodies
375920.statement: Let $K\in\mathcal{K}^d$ be a convex body, and say that a set of directions **illuminates** $K$ if every point of $\operatorname{bd}K$ is illuminated by at least one direction in the set; denote the smallest possible number of directions by $\operatorname{Ill}(K)$. **Illumination conjecture.** Every convex body $K\in\mathcal{K}^d$ can be illuminated by at most $2^d$ directions, and by fewer than $2^d$ directions if $K$ is not a linear image of a $d$-dimensional cube. This is a central problem in convex geometry concerning the illumination number of convex bodies. The source presents it as Boltyanskii's conjecture; no resolution is supplied in the text.

375932.title: Kao's conjecture on Hamiltonicity of Cartesian products with odd paths
375932.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with a **$\{P_2,P_3\}$-factor**, meaning a spanning subgraph whose components are copies of $P_2$ or $P_3$, and let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices. Write $\Delta(G)$ for the maximum degree of $G$, and call $G\Box P_n$ **balanced bipartite** when its two bipartition classes have equal cardinality.

**Kao's conjecture.** If $n\geq 4\Delta(G)-2$ and $G\Box P_n$ is balanced bipartite, then $G\Box P_n$ is hamiltonian.

This conjecture concerns Hamilton cycles in Cartesian products of graphs with paths. The surrounding results establish Hamiltonicity under related hypotheses, while the conjecture specifically addresses the odd-path case in which the standard construction using $P_3\Box P_n$ does not apply; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.

Choose odd n>=14 and k even with n<4k. Read alternating endpoint-imbalance induction proving n>=4k contradiction. Ladder diagnostic adds no novelty.

375980.title: Cancellative elements in bend quotients of tropical principal prime ideals
375980.statement:
Let $K$ be a field with valuation $K\to S$, where $S$ is a sub-semifield of $\mathbb{T}$, and let $\mathcal{M}$ be a toric monoid. Let $I\subseteq K[\mathcal{M}]$ be a principal prime ideal containing neither a monomial nor a binomial, and set

$$
J=\operatorname{trop} I\subseteq S[\mathcal{M}].
$$

**Cancellative-elements conjecture.** An element of $S[\mathcal{M}]/\operatorname{Bend}(J)$ is cancellative if and only if it is the image of a term of $S[\mathcal{M}]$.

This gives a concrete description of cancellative elements in the tropical coordinate semirings used to compute total semirings of fractions. The examples motivate the claim, but no proof or resolution is supplied here.

376009.title: Borodin–Kostochka conjecture
376009.statement:
All graphs considered are finite, simple, and undirected. For a graph $G$, let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number, $\omega(G)$ its clique number, and $\Delta(G)$ its maximum degree. **Borodin–Kostochka conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta(G)\geq 9\quad\text{and}\quad \omega(G)\leq \Delta(G)-1,
$$

then

$$
\chi(G)\leq \Delta(G)-1.
$$

This conjecture asks for a strengthening of Brooks' theorem when the maximum degree is at least $9$ and the clique number is strictly smaller than the maximum degree. It remains open in the supplied source context; the paper studies the conjecture for $(P_6,C_4)$-free graphs.

376073.title: Bollobás–Erdős–Tuza conjecture on transversals of maximum independent sets
376073.statement:
Let $0<c<1$ be a constant. For a graph $G$, let $\alpha(G)$ be the size of a largest independent set, and let $h(G)$ be the size of a smallest set meeting every maximum independent set. **Bollobás–Erdős–Tuza maximum conjecture.** If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with

$$
\alpha(G)\geq cn,
$$

then

$$
h(G)=o(n).
$$

The source presents this as a closely related conjecture that has received recent attention; no resolution is given.

376106.title: Friedlander–Iwaniec Conjecture 2 on automorphic summatory errors
376106.statement:
Let $A(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}a(n)n^{-s}$ be an automorphic series of degree $m$ and conductor $D$ in the Friedlander–Iwaniec framework. Define

$$
R_A(x):=\operatorname*{Res}_{s=1}\left(A(s)\frac{x^s}{s}\right),\qquad E_A(x):=\sum_{n\le x}a(n)-R_A(x),
$$

and let $\boldsymbol\kappa=(\kappa_1,\ldots,\kappa_m)$ be the archimedean parameter array.

**Friedlander–Iwaniec Conjecture 2.** For every $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
E_A(x)\ll_{\varepsilon,\boldsymbol\kappa}D^{1/(2m)}x^{(m-1)/(2m)+\varepsilon}.
$$

This is a conjectural optimal-order bound for the error term in the summatory coefficients of an automorphic series. The paper states that the counterexamples invalidate the proposed deduction from Conjecture 1 but do not themselves disprove this conjecture; it remains open in general, with specializations including the Piltz divisor problem.
376106.review_depth: literal statement, raw provenance, bounded history/title screen, primary conjecture/theorem text; selected proof-body reading specified in note

Source counterexamples address deduction from Conjecture1, expressly not this full error bound. Need analytic cancellation or a genuine family violating the stated conductor exponent.

376118.title: Bang-Jensen–DeVos–Mütze conjecture on strong tournaments in semicomplete digraphs
376118.statement:
Let $D$ be a **semicomplete digraph**, meaning that for every pair of distinct vertices, at least one of the two possible directed arcs is present. A digraph is **$k$-strong** if it has at least $k+1$ vertices and remains strongly connected after the deletion of any subset of $k-1$ vertices. A **tournament** is an oriented complete graph, and a spanning subdigraph contains all vertices of $D$.

**Bang-Jensen–DeVos–Mütze conjecture.** Every $(2k-1)$-strong semicomplete digraph on at least $2k+1$ vertices contains a spanning $k$-strong tournament.

The source presents this as a conjecture supported by its arc-connectivity analogue, while also giving sharpness results for the order and connectivity bounds and a counterexample for a broader class of almost semicomplete digraphs. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

376125.title: Fixed-degree NP-completeness conjecture for non-synchronizing colorings
376125.statement:
Let $G$ be a primitive $k$-out graph, meaning a finite directed graph in which every vertex has out-degree $k$ and whose associated transition structure is primitive. Let $\mathcal C(G)$ be the set of colorings of $G$, and define 
$$
\#\mathrm{NSC}(G):=\bigl|\{\chi\in\mathcal C(G):\chi(G)\text{ is non-synchronizing}\}\bigr|.
$$
 

**Fixed-degree counting conjecture.** The counting problem 
$$
G\longmapsto\#\mathrm{NSC}(G)
$$
 is $\#P$-complete on the class of primitive $k$-out graphs, and remains $\#P$-complete for fixed out-degree $k$, already for $k=2$.

This is presented after a proof of the corresponding decision problem and concerns the exact number of non-synchronizing colorings. The source provides no resolution status for this counting claim.

Finite counts cannot decide complexity. Need a parsimonious or suitable counting reduction preserving primitivity and fixed k2; source leaves this unproved.

376134.title: Akiyama–Watanabe–Albertson–Hass conjecture for bipartite planar graphs
376134.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite planar graph, and let $\mathrm{fvs}(G)$ denote the minimum size of a feedback vertex set of $G$, that is, a vertex set whose deletion leaves a forest.

**Akiyama–Watanabe–Albertson–Hass conjecture.** Every bipartite planar graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\mathrm{fvs}(G)\leq \frac{3v(G)}{8}.
$$

The source describes this as an open conjecture. The current best bound given there is $\mathrm{fvs}(G)\leq (3v(G)-3)/7$, which does not establish the conjectured bound.

376135.title: Dross–Montassier–Pinlou conjecture on feedback vertex sets in large-girth planar graphs
376135.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph of girth at least $g$, and let $e(G)$ be its number of edges. Let $\mathrm{fvs}(G)$ denote the minimum size of a feedback vertex set of $G$, that is, a vertex set whose deletion leaves a forest.

**Dross–Montassier–Pinlou conjecture.** Every planar graph $G$ of girth at least $g$ satisfies

$$
\mathrm{fvs}(G)\leq \frac{e(G)}{g}.
$$

The abstract states that this conjecture is confirmed in the paper, so it is solved.

376146.title: Yau's pinching problem for sectional and normalized scalar curvature
376146.statement:
Let $(M^{n},g)$ be a closed, simply connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge 4$. Define the minimum sectional curvature and normalized scalar curvature at $x\in M$ by

$$
K_{\min}(x)=\min_{\sigma\subset T_xM}K(\sigma),\qquad S_0(x)=\frac{\operatorname{Scal}(M^n)|_x}{n(n-1)}.
$$

Here $S_0$ is the average of the sectional curvatures at a point. **Yau's pinching problem.** If

$$
K_{\min}>\frac{n-1}{n+2}S_0,
$$

pointwise, then $M^n$ is homeomorphic to the $n$-sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$. This is the proposed sectional-scalar curvature analogue of the sphere theorem; the supplied material does not establish whether the sharp formulation is resolved.

376188.statement:

$$
 This would improve the known upper bound $\Delta_{\mathrm H}(n)\le n^{-7/6+o(1)}$ and reflects the expectation that the sharp $2/3$ exponent for the minimal point–line distance problem does not settle the Heilbronn triangle problem.

376195.title: Andrews' local-minimum conjecture for coefficients of $v_1(q)$
376195.statement:
Let

$$
v_1(q)=\sum_{n\geq 0}V_1(n)q^n,
$$

and let $(N_k)_{k\geq 5}$ be the infinite sequence specified in Andrews' same-sign triple conjecture. The sequence of absolute values is

$$
\bigl(\abs{V_1(n)}\bigr)_{n\geq 0}.
$$

**Andrews' local-minimum conjecture.** The three numbers

$$
\abs{V_1(N_k)},\quad \abs{V_1(N_k+1)},\quad \abs{V_1(N_k+2)}
$$

contain a local minimum of this sequence.

This conjecture refines the preceding same-sign triple conjecture by asserting local minimality at the corresponding indices; the supplied source gives no resolution.

376236.title: Catalan classification conjecture for extremal even-intersecting lattice-path families
376236.statement:
Let a lattice path from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$ be a word in $\{E,N\}^{2n}$, and say that two paths are **even-intersecting** if they have an even number of common edges. Let $C_n$ denote the $n$th Catalan number.

**Catalan classification conjecture.** There are exactly $C_n$ families of size $2^n$ in which every two distinct paths have an even number of common edges.

The even-intersection theorem shows that $2^n$ is the maximum possible size, while the paper constructs at least $C_n$ distinct extremal families, one for each noncrossing perfect matching of $[2n]$. The conjecture asserts that these constructions exhaust all extremal families.

376237.title: Wegner's conjecture on the 2-distance chromatic number of planar graphs
376237.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\chi_2(G)$ denote the minimum number of colors in a coloring in which vertices at distance at most $2$ receive distinct colors. **Wegner's conjecture.**

$$
\chi_2(G)\leq 7 \quad\text{if } \Delta=3,
$$

$$
\chi_2(G)\leq \Delta+5 \quad\text{if } 4\leq\Delta\leq 7,
$$

and

$$
\chi_2(G)\leq \left\lfloor\frac{3\Delta}{2}\right\rfloor+1 \quad\text{if } \Delta\geq 8.
$$

The conjecture remains largely open: the source states that the case $\Delta=3$ was proved by Thomassen, while various weaker upper bounds are known for larger maximum degrees.

376249.title: Depth-six classification conjecture for unramified multiple mixed values
376249.statement: Let $M(\bs;\varepsilon)$ denote a multiple mixed value and $T(\bs)$ a multiple t-value. Classify indices as wide, slender, or narrow according to whether their largest component is at least $4$, equal to $3$, or at most $2$. **Depth-six-and-higher MMV classification conjecture.** Suppose that the depth is at least $6$. Then all unramified wide MMVs are MZVs or MtVs, so their parity patterns are $(1,\dots,1)$ or $(-1,\dots,-1)$. All unramified slender MMVs are MZVs, MtVs, or the MTVs given in the width classification conjecture. All unramified narrow MMVs are MZVs, MtVs, the MTVs given in that conjecture, or elements in the three unramified families given by the cited theorems. This conjecture extends the proposed depth-four and depth-five classifications to all greater depths.

376257.title: Gerbner–Palmer's generalized Turán conjecture for trees
376257.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $k$ vertices and let $r\geq3$. Write

$$
n=a(k-1)+b,\qquad 0\leq b<k-1.
$$

For a graph $G$, let ${\mathcal N}(K_r,G)$ denote the number of copies of $K_r$ in $G$, and let ${\mathrm{ex}}(n,K_r,T)$ be the maximum of this number over all $n$-vertex $T$-free graphs. **Gerbner–Palmer's conjecture.**

$$
{\mathrm{ex}}(n,K_r,T)={\mathcal N}\bigl(K_r,aK_{k-1}\cup K_b\bigr)=a\binom{k-1}{r}+\binom{b}{r}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that $aK_{k-1}\cup K_b$ maximizes the number of $r$-cliques among all $n$-vertex $T$-free graphs. The paper verifies it for $r=k-2$ and for $r=k-3\geq5$, but the general statement remains open in the supplied source.

376280.title: Stein's pseudo-semidegree conjecture for long antipaths
376280.statement: Let $G$ be an oriented graph. Its **minimum pseudo-semidegree** $\bar{\delta}^0(G)$ is the minimum among all non-zero in-degrees and out-degrees of its vertices; equivalently, it is the maximum $k$ such that every vertex has either out-degree $0$ or at least $k$, and either in-degree $0$ or at least $k$. **Stein's pseudo-semidegree conjecture.** If $\bar{\delta}^0(G)\geq k$, then $G$ contains an antipath of length $2k-1$. Here an antipath is an oriented path in which every vertex has in-degree $0$ or out-degree $0$. The paper investigates this conjecture for antipaths and proves that every oriented graph with minimum semidegree at least $k$ contains an antipath of length $2k-1$, but the supplied text does not state that the full pseudo-semidegree conjecture is resolved.

376305.title: Frankl–Kupavskii weighted-construction conjecture for the Erdős–Kleitman problem
376305.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, let $e(n,s)$ be the maximum of $|\mathcal F|$ over families $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ with matching number $\nu(\mathcal F)<s$, and, for a weight function $w\colon[n]\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$, define

$$
\mathcal F(w)=\left\{F\subseteq[n]\colon\sum_{x\in F}w(x)\ge1\right\}.
$$

If $\sum_{i=1}^n w(i)<s$, then $\nu(\mathcal F(w))<s$. **Frankl–Kupavskii conjecture.** For any $n,s$, the maximum in the definition of $e(n,s)$ is attained by a family $\mathcal F(w)$ for some $w\colon[n]\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$. This meta-conjecture would reduce the Erdős–Kleitman extremal problem to weighted constructions; its resolution is not specified in the source.

376334.title: Pokrovskiy–Sudakov cycle Ramsey goodness conjecture
376334.statement:
Let $R(G,H)$ denote the two-colour Ramsey number, let $C_n$ be the cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $chi(H)$ and $sigma(H)$ denote the chromatic number and minimum colour-class size of $H$, respectively. **Pokrovskiy–Sudakov conjecture.** There exists $C>0$ such that if $H$ is a graph and $n\geq C|H|$, then 
$$
R(C_n,H)=(\chi(H)-1)(n-1)+\sigma(H).
$$
 The source presents this as open and notes its relation to a conjecture of Allen, Brightwell and Skokan.

376380.title: Sedlar–Škrekovski's mixed metric dimension conjecture
376380.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph that is not a cycle. Write $O(G)=V(G)\cup E(G)$, let $\operatorname{dim_m}(G)$ denote the minimum cardinality of a mixed metric generator of $G$, let $\ell(G)$ be the number of leaves of $G$, and let

$$
c(G)=|E(G)|-|V(G)|+1
$$

be its cyclomatic number. **Sedlar–Škrekovski's conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{dim_m}(G)\leq \ell(G)+2c(G).
$$

Sedlar and Škrekovski proposed this bound after determining the mixed metric dimension of unicyclic graphs. The conjecture concerns the mixed metric dimension of connected graphs beyond cycles; its resolution is not established in the supplied source.

376392.title: Frankl's quadratic-threshold conjecture for critical intersecting hypergraphs
376392.statement:
Let $k>t\ge 1$ be integers, let $\mathcal F$ be a $k$-uniform, $t$-intersecting hypergraph, and let $\tau_t(\mathcal F)$ be the minimum size of a set meeting every edge of $\mathcal F$ in at least $t$ vertices. Write $d=k-t$ and define

$$
m(k,t)=\max\{\lvert\mathcal F\rvert:\mathcal F\text{ is }t\text{-intersecting and }t\text{-critical}\},
$$

where $t$-critical means $\tau_t(\mathcal F)=k$.

**Frankl's conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that, whenever $k>c d^2$,

$$
m(k,k-d)=\binom{k+d}{d}.
$$

The complete $k$-graph on a set of $k+d$ vertices attains the lower bound $\binom{k+d}{d}$. Frankl proved the equality for $k\ge d^4$, and also proved the cases $d=1$ and $d=2$; the conjecture predicts a quadratic threshold in $d$ for the same extremal value.

376405.statement:

376562.title: The open O(1) loop-model largest-component conjecture
376562.statement:
Consider the dense O(1) loop model with open boundary conditions and system size $L$, and normalise its groundstate wavefunction so that its smallest element is $1$. Let $N_8(2n)$ count cyclically symmetric transpose-complement plane partitions and let $A_{\rm v}(2n-1)$ count vertically symmetric alternating sign matrices. **The open-loop largest-component conjecture.** The largest element of the wavefunction is $N_8(2n)$ for $L=2n$ and $A_{\rm v}(2n-1)$ for $L=2n-1$.

The O(1) loop model is the real loop counterpart of the corresponding XXZ chain, with loop fugacity $1$. The prediction links its extremal wavefunction component to symmetry classes of plane partitions and alternating sign matrices, and is supported only by the finite tables in the source.

376563.title: The open O(1) loop-model 1-sum conjecture
376563.statement:

$$
S_{2n}^{(1)}=A_{\rm v}(2n+1),
\qquad
S_{2n-1}^{(1)}=N_8(2n).
$$

This is an O(1) loop-model analogue of the XXZ-chain sum formulas and connects the sums to vertically symmetric alternating sign matrices and cyclically symmetric transpose-complement plane partitions. The source offers finite-size evidence but no proof.
